original_card.question: Can a legal decoder or coframe change improve the full signed moment, including changed helper targets?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Price one complete changed itinerary with both paid and productive histograms. Check #5693/#5698 for overlap and their exact hypotheses before another coframe search. Use the signed invoice preflight where its boundary contract agrees; an inconclusive concave comparison is not a power crossing. Stop if an optimistic complete budget fails at the chosen target or native delivery remains unspecified.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.

actual_scope: Can the 40 degree-at-least-2 monomials of the #7031 frame-0 word be named as primitives on the selected #6030 invoice, under the constructors that invoice uses?
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a decoder or coframe change improves the full signed moment. Open PR #7031, question 3, asks a prior naming question: place its 40 charged monomials on the selected #6030 invoice before any profile comparison. This package answers only that naming question.
bottleneck_link: A thirteen-row comparison with the selected profile is not available until each charged monomial has a primitive name on the #6030 invoice. The inherited constructors do not assign those names, so the comparison stays blocked and no kappa is claimed.
stop_rule: Stop when each of the 40 monomials has an inherited primitive name, or when the inherited constructors are shown not to determine such a name. Do not compare thirteen rows with the selected profile and do not change kappa.
evidence: PROOF.md and verify.py. The expansion and the three failed readings are exhaustive finite censuses. The invoice histograms are rebuilt from the selected word. The degree reading is refused because the constructor texts do not read a degree. This is a scoped obstruction, not a kappa.
author: unpaidmoon, with substantial Cursor Grok assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial Cursor Grok assistance. No subagents. The selected word, the PR5827 replay rule, and the #7031 polynomial are used as pinned inputs.

open_questions.question: Which total function from these 40 exponents to the inherited (side, rank) alphabet do the selected constructors determine?
open_questions.why_it_matters: No comparison of thirteen frame rows with the selected profile is available until every charged monomial has one primitive name.
open_questions.first_step: Make one rank constructor read one of these exponents, or show that a constructor already does, and check the image of all 40.
open_questions.blocked_by: The present constructors read frame dimensions, idle lengths, query shears, and one diagonal popcount. They do not read a chart monomial.
